handoffs.change: Record four points. (1) The shot list's tempo travels in the hero button's data-dc-shots, server-rendered from lib/page.ts and lib/film.ts, because browser-data-loader strips tempo, estVh and beats. (2) Star weights and positions come from the live DOM (data-beat-star / data-beat-weight), not from estVh. (3) A scroll star ([data-card-beat], [data-beat-scroll], scrub) dwells where its spotlight range lets go: box bottom at 20% of the viewport, which is a card star's end or the moment the house lights are fully down. A time star dwells centred; 2× halves the dwells. (4) The stop pill is plain DOM in the 'stop' layer, not a React portal.
handoffs.why: These are the implementation's deviations from the spec text.

First-load estimate (gzip of transpiled source, not minified): film-frame +445 B, snitch +214 B, film-beats +140 B, analytics +283 B (mostly dead code in production). Expect about +0.4–0.5 KB gz minified. The house lights, the warm-point carry, the player, the trackers, the dc binder and the chapter select are all lazy. The hero button is server markup (0 JS; about 0.4 KB of HTML for data-dc-shots). app/p3/cinema.css is left with no rules (0 CSS).

Loops: L22 (F-3I) and L23 (F-HP) are registered and accepted. They are not FAILED as the brief says; loopFor lights them up. iconic-express has no loop (L13 failed), so the HP DEFAULT screen uses the code path: push plus depth where a line mark exists.

B30's marker sits above the frame (top −105vh, 40vh tall) so its spotlight ownership ends when the close ends. That lets the B31 title play right after the house lights go down, instead of waiting into its 1.5 s skip. B35's marker sits at the films section's bottom edge.

The director's cut plays from where it is when started within the first viewport (the hero button). Elsewhere it cuts to the top first. Before gliding it waits for a closing menu or palette to release its scroll lock.
The credits 'Libraries' row already reads the credits.libraries copy key. The role label 'Libraries' is a literal like every other role, so no handoff is needed.
New strings: none. Everything uses existing copy keys (dc.*, chapter.*, credits.more.summary). The aria-labels 'Director's cut' and 'Stop' are those keys with the leading glyph removed.
